questions.stem: Which VHF channel is reserved for distress, urgency, safety and calling?
questions.explanation: Channel 16 is the distress, urgency, safety and calling channel. Channel 70 is the DSC alert channel, 21B carries the continuous marine broadcast, and 13 is an intership navigation channel.

options: Digital selective calling (DSC) alerts and calls
questions.explanation: Channel 70 (156.525 MHz) is the DSC alert channel. The radio sends coded calls on it; voice traffic goes on other channels.

questions.stem: A tug skipper wants to call a Coast Guard centre for the first time. Why should the first call be on Channel 16?
options: Working channels are illegal for calls
MCTS centres monitor Channel 16 but do not monitor working channels
Channel 16 is only for voice mail
questions.explanation: The RAMN says initial calls are made on Channel 16 because MCTS centres do not monitor working channels. The reason is monitoring, not signal strength or legality.

questions.stem: Which word announces a message of grave and imminent danger needing immediate assistance?
questions.explanation: MAYDAY is the distress word. PAN PAN is a very urgent message about safety, and SECURITE announces an important navigational or weather warning.

questions.stem: On the BC coast, which channel carries the continuous marine broadcast of weather and warnings?
questions.explanation: The RAMN facilities part shows the BC continuous marine broadcast on Channel 21B, with WX channels also used. Channel 16 is for calling, 70 for DSC.

questions.stem: A vessel is in BC waters outside a traffic zone. Which channel do the regulations name for a navigation safety call?
questions.explanation: Schedule 4 of the NSR 2020 names Channel 16 outside a traffic zone. Channel 13 appears in the Great Lakes entry, not the Pacific.

questions.stem: What is the minimum radio operator certificate needed to operate a marine radio in Canada?
options: No certificate is needed on a commercial vessel
questions.explanation: Anyone operating a marine radio in Canada needs at least an ROC-M; the ROC-MC meets that requirement.

questions.stem: A vessel has a VHF installation. Who on the deck watch must hold an appropriate radio operator certificate?
options: The person in charge of the deck watch
questions.explanation: MPR s. 216(2)(a)(ii) requires the person in charge of the deck watch to hold a radio operator certificate appropriate to the vessel, if it has a VHF installation.

questions.stem: A DSC radio sends an alert that nobody can link to the vessel. What is the most likely fault?
options: The radio was not programmed with the vessel's own nine-digit MMSI
The squelch was set too high
questions.explanation: A DSC radio identifies the vessel by its MMSI. Without the correct nine-digit number the alert cannot be traced.

questions.stem: Except in distress, how much power may a radio installation radiate?
options: No more than needed for clear communication
questions.explanation: NSR 2020 s. 245 limits power to what is needed for clear communication, except in distress.

questions.stem: On lookout you hear 'PAN PAN, PAN PAN, PAN PAN' on Channel 16 from a vessel with engine failure. What do you do?
options: Wait until the end of the watch to mention it
Tell the officer of the watch at once what you heard, including the vessel name and position if caught
questions.explanation: A rating who is not certified listens and reports at once. The officer of the watch decides the response.

questions.stem: Which channel is the intership bridge-to-bridge navigation channel named in the Great Lakes entry of the regulations?
questions.explanation: Channel 13 appears in the Great Lakes entry of Schedule 4; in BC outside a traffic zone the regulations name Channel 16.

questions.stem: Which pairing of word and meaning is correct?
options: PAN PAN: a very urgent message about the safety of a vessel or person; SECURITE: an important navigational or weather warning
PAN PAN: a weather warning; SECURITE: a vessel sinking
SECURITE: grave and imminent danger; MAYDAY: a weather warning
PAN PAN: a routine call; SECURITE: a request for a berth
questions.explanation: RAMN gives these meanings. MAYDAY is the grave and imminent danger word.
